content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question regarding connection between a PLC and software developed by me. I created a circuit in the PLC with one input and one output. How can I establish reliable communication between the PLC and the software? I want to send commands from the software to the PLC and have it execute them. Any advice?

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. The basic PLC module only supports Ethernet TCP/IP using the S7 protocol. Some PLC versions offer additional support for Ethernet TCP/IP with both S7 and Modbus TCP/IP protocols.

Thanks for your reply. I'm not very experienced, as my knowledge comes from a course I took a few years ago. Could you help clarify what I need to do? I've read comments but still don't quite understand. Could you share an example of how to set up Modbus communication? My circuit is simple: one input turns one output (a lamp) on or off, and I want the input to receive a command from the PC.

Did you know this PLC has an integrated web server? This server provides a virtual display and control interface, including button functionality, even if the operator device isn't physically present. The newer PLC versions also offer an extended web server. You can use software such as a web editor to create custom web pages for visualization and device control.
Here's a link to a video explaining how to use the web server for programming tasks. [url]

My colleague created a web page because we wanted something customized. He is experienced and told me which bits and bytes to read or write. However, he doesn't want to explain how Modbus works in detail.
Sorry, I'm unable to help with that. You may want to consider open source tools such as Snap7 for your project.
Thank you very much for your efforts.

Hello, I'm confused because some users set up Modbus using the 'tool > ethernet connection > Modbus client' tab, while others use the 'network project' tab. Are both methods equivalent and practical? I designed my circuit but couldn't test it yet. When I try to connect using software like Modbus Poll, I have trouble figuring out a successful setup. I want to control coil 1 from the PC, setting its value to 0 or 1, and use v0.0 to change the value.

You configured your PLC as a Modbus TCP client. If your connected device is set as a Modbus TCP server, then you're on the right track. Remember, the PLC can function as both client and server. Here's an example for Modbus and the PLC: [url]
So, I have two designs—are both correct and valid? If my circuit is okay, the other person can set up Modbus. I want to make sure my circuit is designed properly. Thanks for your help.

I have two circuits now; are they both correct? I want confirmation that my design is suitable before showing it to my software developer. Could you review my programs and let me know if everything looks good? I appreciate your support.

There are various ways to set up Modbus communication. The approach in your configuration file might be best, depending on the user's experience. If you need to transfer more signals, you can do so in one block. You don't need separate network inputs for outputs; simply use the proper coil number for outputs. If you need both local and remote control, use an OR block to switch outputs with either a button or network input. See the attached Modbus chart for details. Depending on your PC, use numbers starting at 0 or 1—set this in the spreadsheet. It's generally easier if you set the PLC as a server (slave) and the PC as a client (master). Then, just activate the slave in the PLC program. For digital signals, use variables like Vx.y or Mx, and for analog signals, use VWx or AMx. These signals can be chosen easily by the PC client.
Thank you for your reply. Based on your answer, if I use Vx.y or VWx.y, do I just have to use the correct coil, or do I need to activate something additionally?
You need to activate the Modbus server in the PLC, and optionally set your PC's IP address for more security, allowing only your PC to connect. See the attached example with comments.
Thank you for your effort and time. As a beginner, I appreciate your help.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users often face difficulty when trying to connect third-party or custom applications to PLCs, especially for external control functions. There is widespread confusion about configuration steps and communication protocols (S7, Modbus TCP/IP), and uncertainty about which setup options are interchangeable. These challenges result in high barriers to effective self-learning and usability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek clear, step-by-step guidance on setting up protocol-based communication (S7 or Modbus TCP/IP) between PC applications and PLC hardware. They expect simple configuration instructions and an easy way to achieve reliable external control from their software.
